title: D-001: Agent-First Architecture
body:
# D-001: Agent-First Architecture

**Date:** 2026-03-28
**Status:** Active

## Decision

Build the framework for AI agents as primary operators, not humans as typists. All commands, schemas, and workflows are designed to be executed autonomously.

## Why

Human-first writing tools exist in abundance. The gap is in orchestrated, quality-gated, multi-phase document production that agents can drive end-to-end. Designing for agents first means every interface is explicit, structured, and inspectable — which also makes it better for humans when they do intervene.

Agent-first design produces different architectural choices than human-first design. Commands must have structured inputs and outputs because agents cannot guess from context. Handoffs must use defined schemas because agents cannot negotiate informally. Quality gates must be explicit because agents cannot apply implicit judgment. All of these characteristics — which serve agents — also serve humans who want to understand what the system is doing and why.

## Alternatives Considered

**Human-in-the-loop tool with AI assistance.** Rejected because it constrains the autonomy model and produces different architectural choices: UI over CLI, interactive over batch, single-pass over multi-phase. A human-in-the-loop tool assumes a human operator at every step. The agent-first architecture allows human intervention at any step but does not require it. The human-first alternative would have required fundamentally different command design — interactive, stateful, session-oriented — rather than the batch, resumable, schema-validated design this framework uses.

## Consequences

Every command must have structured inputs and outputs. Vague "just do your best" commands are not allowed. All handoffs between agents must use defined schemas. This has implications throughout the framework: schema definitions become first-class deliverables (D-006), agent specs must be precise about inputs and outputs (D-007), and quality gates must be evaluable without human interpretation (D-008). The agent-first architecture is the root decision from which most other architectural choices follow.
